metadata.title: Getting Skills Right: Trends in Adult Learning: New Data from the 2023 Survey of Adult Skills

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PIAAC thematic report synthesises results from the 2023 Survey of Adult Skills across participating countries. The underlying survey is designed to produce cross-country comparable estimates of adult proficiency (literacy, numeracy, adaptive problem solving) and related learning participation, typically requiring complex survey weighting to reflect sampling probabilities and nonresponse. The excerpt provided does not specify the exact weight variable names or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used, so the precise implementation cannot be confirmed from the text shown. For users working with the microdata, the appropriate approach is to apply the official PIAAC/Survey of Adult Skills sampling weights supplied with the dataset and to follow the accompanying technical documentation for variance estimation; if weights are not applied, estimates may be biased and standard errors may be misestimated.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a thematic OECD report describing trends and policy-relevant patterns from the 2023 Survey of Adult Skills rather than presenting an empirical student-level predictive modeling analysis with explicitly documented plausible-value (PV) procedures. Plausible values are typically relevant for cognitive achievement domains in PIAAC, but the provided excerpt does not report the PV handling method (e.g., Rubin’s rules, PV averaging) and does not describe a specific analytic pipeline that would require PV documentation. Missing-data handling is likewise not described in the excerpt because the report focuses on descriptive trend reporting and policy synthesis rather than a fully specified statistical estimation procedure.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the 2023 Survey of Adult Skills data from countries participating in the OECD Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC) Board of Participating Countries (BPC). The excerpt does not specify the analytic inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., age bands, literacy/numeracy domain availability, or any subsample restrictions), so the exact filtering criteria cannot be extracted from the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD thematic report (“Getting Skills Right”) describes trends in adult learning using new data from the 2023 Survey of Adult Skills, prepared under the OECD Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC) Board of Participating Countries. It focuses on where, what, and how adults learn, examining participation in formal, non-formal, and informal learning, the content and intensity/modes of learning, and barriers that limit access—especially for disadvantaged groups. The report also links these patterns to how policies and practices could be redesigned to better support adult learners in a changing labour market. The excerpt does not provide the report’s specific statistical model outputs or performance metrics, and it does not document PV handling or missing-data procedures, so the extraction here is limited to the assessment purpose and scope rather than quantitative ML results.
